frequency_question: How often do major energy/infrastructure reform packages passed by Congress successfully incorporate specific textual provisions for interstate permitting without falling afoul of technical drafting exclusions?
membership_rule: Members are federal statutory packages enacted since 1995 containing multiple cross-sector energy or infrastructure permitting provisions. Excluded are single-project waivers, non-statutory resolutions, and purely appropriations-based riders.

cases.name: Energy Independence and Security Act of 2007
Fixing America's Surface Transportation (FAST) Act (Title XI)

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 5 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 5 major bipartisan infrastructure/energy permitting legislative vehicles identified since 1995; all successfully met structural drafting standards for interstate infrastructure when enacted.
known_gaps: Excludes minor standalone pipeline riders that failed to pass independently.
skeleton: Comprehensive energy/infrastructure bills enacted in a divided or polarized legislative environment typically undergo rigorous legal scrubbing to ensure statutory definitions match the required textual criteria for interstate permitting.
multiplier: 5 hits / 5 cases = 1.00 base rate for matching criteria once the substantive event of enactment occurs.
validity_reason: Legislative drafting standards and the structure of omnibus reconciliation/infrastructure packages remain stable across congressional sessions.
